Game runtime.summary: Start a game, coordinate its session, and move between worlds.
Game runtime.description: Use [Game] to configure a solo, LAN, or Steam game from an existing scene owner. Use [GameConfig] to attach a dedicated server with [code]boot_server(owner)[/code]. For a coordinated game, register [WorldDefinition] destinations and use [GameScenes] for travel.

Code-first game.summary: Configure, attach, and run a game from GDScript.
Code-first game.description: Call [code]Game.configure(level, player).boot(self)[/code] from a live scene owner. Await the direct game actions for a typed [GameResult]. Use [GameProvider] and [GameBindings] to supply a custom session transport at boot.

Lower-level runtime.summary: Work with existing game definitions, operation handles, and provider services.
Lower-level runtime.description: Use [GameRuntime] and [GameDefinition] for existing scenes and lower-level integrations. These classes expose retained operations, admission rules, and provider interfaces. [GameConfig] can adapt a legacy definition before you move callers to [Game].

Steam multiplayer.summary: Connect a Crimson game session to Steam for hosting, discovery, and joining.
Steam multiplayer.description: Choose [code]Game.configure(level, player).steam().boot(self)[/code] to use Steam hosting and discovery. Use the [Game] actions for quick join and exact invite acceptance, and [code]game.steam()[/code] for client services. [SteamProvider], [GameInvites], and [SteamServices] expose the lower-level attachment and dedicated status interfaces.

World sessions.summary: Run a standalone session in one configured world.
World sessions.description: [WorldSession] and [WorldSessionDefinition] support existing standalone fixed-world integrations. Use [Game] for a new project, with ordinary [Marker3D] children under [code]SpawnPoints[/code] and one [Camera3D] in the player scene. Existing [PlayerSpawnPoint] and [LocalPlayerView] placements remain supported.

Inventory.summary: Place, move, and exchange game items across inventory grids.
Inventory.description: Start a standalone grid with [code]Inventory.grid(size)[/code] and add items by ID and footprint. Read their placements as [InventoryItemView] values. In coordinated games, use [InventoryConfig] to enable backpacks and provide pickup rules. A [MatchInventory] backpack places an authorized pickup and consumes it in one commit. [SpatialInventory] and the lower-level adapters provide explicit placement, equipment, container, sorting, and trade tools.

Match runtime.summary: Coordinate authoritative game state and route player commands.
Match runtime.description: Use the transaction coordinator to prepare, validate, and publish changes across game state stores. Player bindings map admitted peers to stable player IDs, possession tracks primary control, and the command router checks the match and player context before calling your gameplay handler.

Replication.summary: Synchronize each peer's view of committed game state.
Replication.description: Use StateReplication to send an initial snapshot and subsequent changes to admitted peers in a Godot multiplayer scope. The game decides which state each recipient can see. Clients read the resulting projection and track when it is ready for the current world.

Save and restore.summary: Capture checkpoints, inspect saved generations, and restore game state.
Save and restore.description: Select a coordinated game's checkpoint slot through [code]game.save_slot(profile, slot)[/code]. [SaveSlot] and [SaveRequest] expose the slot's operations. Use [SaveCoordinator] to configure participant capture, migrations, and staged restores directly. [SavePresentation] provides metadata helpers for checkpoint menus.

Scene loading.summary: Load a registered world offline or coordinate its replacement across peers.
Scene loading.description: Use [GameScenes] to travel to registered worlds in a coordinated game. [SceneLoadManager] provides lower-level control over world replacement. Register scene IDs, choose a world container, and request a local or coordinated load. The manager prepares the scene asynchronously and reports completion or failure.

Sessions and transport.summary: Open offline and network sessions with configurable transport and admission.
Sessions and transport.description: Use [Game] with [code].lan()[/code] for direct hosting and joining. The lower-level [GameSession] API opens offline and network sessions over Godot multiplayer. ENet is the default direct transport. Supply a custom [SessionTransport] through [GameBindings], or use [SessionAuthenticator] when a lower-level integration verifies connection proofs and resolves identities.

Steamworks.summary: Use Steam client and game server capabilities from Godot.
Steamworks.description: Attach app features to an existing owner with [code]Steamworks.boot(self)[/code], or get the exact Steam game attachment from [code]game.steam()[/code]. [SteamConfig] sets the expected AppID and discovery options. Pick a service below for the capabilities your game needs.

Client and results.summary: Start a Steam client and inspect the results of Steam operations.
Client and results.description: Use [Steamworks] to start a standalone attachment or access the client services attached to a game. [SteamClient] is the lower-level callback node for existing integrations. This area also contains app and DLC metadata, platform utilities, and the result and operation types returned by Steam actions.

Lobbies and social.summary: Discover lobbies and parties, read friends, and update Steam presence.
Lobbies and social.description: Use the lobby and party services to discover sessions or manage a social lobby. Use the friends, presence, and overlay services to display player status, expose join options, and open Steam panes.

Servers and networking.summary: Discover dedicated servers, inspect network paths, and exchange Steam packets.
Servers and networking.description: Configure dedicated servers and search their listings, or use standalone Steam sockets and scoped messages for your own network traffic. The networking classes expose relay and connection observations. A Steam game server can read and update progression for authenticated players.

Stats and leaderboards.summary: Read or update player progression and work with Steam leaderboards.
Stats and leaderboards.description: Use [Steamworks] to request the achievement panel and [SteamAchievements] to submit an unlock. Steam separately handles display and persistence. The stats and leaderboard services read or update progression, fetch score pages, and submit scores. Use the trusted publisher service if the backend owns score submission.

Inventory and purchases.summary: Read the player's Steam inventory and start purchases through your backend.
Inventory and purchases.description: Use Steam Inventory to inspect item definitions and stacks and request supported item changes. The client purchase service reads offers and follows orders through your game's authenticated commerce backend. The backend controls prices, settlement, and fulfillment.

Cloud and Workshop.summary: Store files in Steam Cloud and work with Steam Workshop items.
Cloud and Workshop.description: Use Steam Cloud to read and write app files, inspect quota, and work with shared files. Use Workshop to discover, subscribe to, and inspect installed items, or to publish and update content for your app.

Input and device.summary: Read Steam Input, device information, and Remote Play sessions.
Input and device.description: Use Steam Input to resolve connected controllers and sample your game's action bindings. Device classes report hardware and VR state and can show Steam's text input. Remote Play classes expose connected streams, invitations, and optional stream input.

Media and voice.summary: Integrate Steam capture, recording, playback, and voice features.
Media and voice.description: Capture and annotate screenshots, add gameplay markers to Steam Game Recording, and inspect available media and broadcast state. The voice service captures microphone audio with player consent and decodes incoming Steam voice frames.

Auth, HTTP, and diagnostics.summary: Request Steam tickets, use Steam web services, and inspect SDK diagnostics.
Auth, HTTP, and diagnostics.description: Request Web API or encrypted app tickets for verification by a trusted backend. Use the HTTP and offscreen browser classes for requests and game-owned web pages. Use diagnostics to capture Steam SDK messages while investigating a client issue.

Steam publisher.summary: Call authorized Steam publisher services from a trusted backend.
Steam publisher.description: Use the separate trusted publisher addon in a backend or operator project that holds your Steam publisher credentials. These services verify player tickets and ownership, process orders and inventory changes, manage notifications, and perform authorized leaderboard and moderation actions.

Host and authorization.summary: Configure the publisher scope and verify Steam identities and ownership.
Host and authorization.description: Use the publisher host and settings to resolve secrets in your backend and initialize its Steam Web API scope. Verify client tickets before trusting an account identity. Query current ownership or verify encrypted app tickets with the required key and challenge store.

Commerce and inventory.summary: Settle Steam Wallet orders and perform trusted inventory actions.
Commerce and inventory.description: Use the publisher purchase service to quote, finalize, reconcile, and refund orders for verified players. Implement the purchase store to persist orders and apply entitlements. Use publisher inventory to read or change inventory and open supported trades.

Notifications.summary: Manage asynchronous game sessions and Steam notification consent.
Notifications.description: Use the notification service to request opt-in and create or update asynchronous game sessions for verified participants. Supply localized text and participant state. The backend's notification store persists session ownership and consent request decisions.

Moderation and leaderboards.summary: Apply app-scoped moderation and submit backend-verified scores.
Moderation and leaderboards.description: Use the moderation service to report findings, review reports, and request or remove sanctions after your game policy authorizes them. Use the publisher leaderboard service to submit scores from runs your backend has validated.
